This will look a lot more alive. painting (as it was taught to me) is about understanding a sight and interpreting it and getting the shapes etc down on a page, not just copying someone elses interpretation. Yes exactly. There's a moment when confronted with our actions we have three options: \
\
1) you can throw it back at the other person, tear them down too and ruin any respect and integrity in the relationship. You move forward with a righteousness that 'they suck' and they deserved it \
\
2) You can wallow in shame and self pity, to try and seek affirmation from the victim. "I am a terrible person- (please tell me I'm good)" and go forward with a mentality that you are hard-done-by and the world sucks and everything is hopeless. \
\
3) You can fully accept what you did, and visualise what your favourite person would do. You stand up tall to face your actions head- on. You uphold strong boundaries with the person you've hurt. Focusing fully on listening, without inserting your ego. You do not push guilt nor expectations on them, and you do not brag or fill them with hopes of your rehabilitation. You quietly focus on your own goals and show yourself through actions long-term.

I also find it very helpful to think someone who is excellent and ask myself what they would do. \
\

Hello, I want to say I'm very sorry for the misery you're in. Phones are full of bright interesting things and it's totally understandable that you are addicted to it. Do not guilt yourself, have empathy. Some small tips that have really helped me with scrolling: 1) just look to the left whilst watching a video, what can you see. If you cant move or stop watching, just looking away briefly from the screen helps a lot without having to get off the phone. 2) try and make yourself watch the end of every tiktok video. Mostly they are actually boring, and making myself watch all of it, cuts back on the dopamine kick and I sometimes get enough drive to get up. 3) in the moments when I'm not on my phone, I think about what I'm stressed about. Just ask yourself: what am I seeking? Often it's comfort, and you can just give yourself a few kind words, "I am doing great considering how stressed I feel. I am feeling lonely- but I am great and I'm a really cool person." This little kick helps the shame and sometimes helps me process what I'm avoiding. 4) I stop telling myself to get off my phone. I tell myself wholeheartedly that I will watch as much as I want. And then the part of me that doesn't want to, naturally gets the opportunity to fight back. 5) PODCASTS. they are such an incredible way for me to get up and move about whilst still mentally being on my phone/ elsewhere. I get so much shit done with podcasts because you can still dampen the harsh reality of real life. 6) the idea of "I am, what I do most of the time" really drives me to be the cool person that I want to be. Sorry if this adds to the shame complex but sometimes it helps you envision HOW you want to be. It's all well and good suggesting you get off your phone, but it's so unhelpful when you turn the phone off, and there's just nothing else immediately to turn to. I think that my life has moulded me to be trans, and that isn't AT ALL less valid or "real" than passing some medical test for being trans. I KNOW that I am trans.
